q-126913.name: Question 1
q-126913.problem:
The closed, positively oriented curve $C$ is defined as $r(t)=9\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+5\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j$ for $t\in [0,2\pi ).$ The outward-pointing unit normal vector on $C$ can be expressed as

$$
n=\frac{a(t)\,i+b(t)\,j}{||{r}^{′}(t)||}.
$$

Find the function $a(t).$
q-126913.worked_solution:
For convenience, we express $r(t)$ in column vector notation:

$$
r(t)=[\begin{aligned}x(t) \\ y(t)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}9\operatorname{cos}⁡t \\ 5\operatorname{sin}⁡t\end{aligned}]
$$

To calculate the outward-pointing normal vector of a closed, positively oriented curve, we follow three steps:

**Step 1**: We compute the tangent vector ${r}^{′}(t).$

Differentiating the expression for $r(t),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =[\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t) \\ {y}^{′}(t)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-9\operatorname{sin}⁡t \\ 5\operatorname{cos}⁡t\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 2**: Since $C$ is oriented counterclockwise, we rotate ${r}^{′}(t)$ by ${90}^{∘}$ *clockwise* to obtain an outward-pointing normal vector.

The rotation matrix that corresponds to a ${90}^{∘}$ clockwise rotation is

$$
R=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Rotating the vector ${r}^{′}(t)$ by ${90}^{∘}$ clockwise, we get

$$
[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-9\operatorname{sin}⁡t \\ 5\operatorname{cos}⁡t\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}5\operatorname{cos}⁡t \\ 9\operatorname{sin}⁡t\end{aligned}].
$$

**Step 3**: Finally, we normalize the vector found in step 2.

Note that the magnitude of the vector found in step 2 equals the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(t)$ (since they differ only by a rotation). Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}n & =\frac{1}{||{r}^{′}(t)||}[\begin{aligned}5\operatorname{cos}⁡t \\ 9\operatorname{sin}⁡t\end{aligned}]=\frac{5\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,i+9\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,j}{||{r}^{′}(t)||}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we conclude that $a(t)=5\operatorname{cos}⁡t.$

n=a(t)i+b(t)j||r′(t)||. Find the function a(t).

a

−9cos⁡t
c
5cos⁡t

R=[01−10].

Rotating the vector r′(t) by 90∘ clockwise, we get

[01−10][−9sin⁡t5cos⁡t]=[5cos⁡t9sin⁡t].

q-126926.problem:
The closed curve $C$ is defined as $r(t)=9\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+10\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j$ for $t\in [0,2\pi ).$ The outward-pointing unit normal vector for $C$ can be expressed as

$$
n=\frac{a(t)\,i+b(t)\,j}{||{r}^{′}(t)||}.
$$

*Hint: Observe that $C$ is traversed clockwise.*

$$
r(t)=[\begin{aligned}x(t) \\ y(t)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}9\operatorname{sin}⁡t \\ 10\operatorname{cos}⁡t\end{aligned}]
$$

**Step 1**: We compute the tangent vector ${r}^{′}(t).$

Differentiating the expression for $r(t),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =[\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t) \\ {y}^{′}(t)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}9\operatorname{cos}⁡t \\ -10\operatorname{sin}⁡t\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 2**: Since $C$ is oriented clockwise, we rotate ${r}^{′}(t)$ by ${90}^{∘}$ *counterclockwise* to obtain an outward-pointing normal vector.

The rotation matrix that corresponds to a ${90}^{∘}$ counterclockwise rotation is

$$
R=[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Rotating the vector ${r}^{′}(t)$ by ${90}^{∘}$ counterclockwise, we get

$$
[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}9\operatorname{cos}⁡t \\ -10\operatorname{sin}⁡t\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}10\operatorname{sin}⁡t \\ 9\operatorname{cos}⁡t\end{aligned}].
$$

**Step 3**: Finally, we normalize the vector found in step 2.

Note that the magnitude of the vector found in step 2 equals the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(t)$ (since they differ only by a rotation). Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}n & =\frac{1}{||{r}^{′}(t)||}[\begin{aligned}10\operatorname{sin}⁡t \\ 9\operatorname{cos}⁡t\end{aligned}]=\frac{10\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+9\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j}{||{r}^{′}(t)||}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we conclude that $a(t)=10\operatorname{sin}⁡t.$

The closed, positively oriented curve C is defined as r(t)=5cos⁡ti+3sin⁡tj for t∈[0,2π). The outward-pointing unit normal vector on C can be expressed as

n=a(t)i+b(t)j||r′(t)||. Find the function a(t).

a
−5sin⁡t
b
5sin⁡t
c
−3cos⁡t
d
3sin⁡t
e
3cos⁡t
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

For convenience, we express r(t) in column vector notation:

r(t)=[x(t)y(t)]=[5cos⁡t3sin⁡t]

To calculate the outward-pointing normal vector of a closed, positively oriented curve, we follow three steps:

Step 1: We compute the tangent vector r′(t).

Differentiating the expression for r(t), we get

r′(t)=[x′(t)y′(t)]=[−5sin⁡t3cos⁡t].

Step 2: Since C is oriented counterclockwise, we rotate r′(t) by 90∘ clockwise to obtain an outward-pointing normal vector.

The rotation matrix that corresponds to a 90∘ clockwise rotation is

[01−10].

Rotating the vector r′(t) by 90∘ clockwise, we get

[01−10][−5sin⁡t3cos⁡t]=[3cos⁡t5sin⁡t].

Step 3: Finally, we normalize the vector found in step 2.

Note that the magnitude of the vector found in step 2 equals the magnitude of r′(t) (since they differ only by a rotation). Therefore,

n=1||r′(t)||[3cos⁡t5sin⁡t]=3cos⁡ti+5sin⁡tj||r′(t)||.

Finally, we conclude that a(t)=3cos⁡t.

q-149686.name: Question 4
q-149686.problem:
The closed curve $C$ is defined as $r(t)=8\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+5\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j$ for $t\in [0,2\pi ).$ The outward-pointing unit normal vector for $C$ can be expressed as

$$
n=\frac{a(t)\,i+b(t)\,j}{||{r}^{′}(t)||}.
$$

Find the function $a(t).$

*Hint: Observe that $C$ is traversed clockwise.*
q-149686.worked_solution:
For convenience, we express $r(t)$ in column vector notation:

$$
r(t)=[\begin{aligned}x(t) \\ y(t)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}8\operatorname{sin}⁡t \\ 5\operatorname{cos}⁡t\end{aligned}]
$$

To calculate the outward-pointing normal vector of a closed, *negatively* oriented curve, we follow three steps:

**Step 1**: We compute the tangent vector ${r}^{′}(t).$

Differentiating the expression for $r(t),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =[\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t) \\ {y}^{′}(t)\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}8\operatorname{cos}⁡t \\ -5\operatorname{sin}⁡t\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 2**: Since $C$ is oriented clockwise, we rotate ${r}^{′}(t)$ by ${90}^{∘}$ *counterclockwise* to obtain an outward-pointing normal vector.

The rotation matrix that corresponds to a ${90}^{∘}$ counterclockwise rotation is

$$
R=[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Rotating the vector ${r}^{′}(t)$ by ${90}^{∘}$ counterclockwise, we get

$$
[\begin{aligned}0 & -1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}8\operatorname{cos}⁡t \\ -5\operatorname{sin}⁡t\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}5\operatorname{sin}⁡t \\ 8\operatorname{cos}⁡t\end{aligned}].
$$

**Step 3**: Finally, we normalize the vector found in step 2.

Note that the magnitude of the vector found in step 2 equals the magnitude of ${r}^{′}(t)$ (since they differ only by a rotation). Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}n & =\frac{1}{||{r}^{′}(t)||}[\begin{aligned}5\operatorname{sin}⁡t \\ 8\operatorname{cos}⁡t\end{aligned}]=\frac{5\operatorname{sin}⁡t\,i+8\operatorname{cos}⁡t\,j}{||{r}^{′}(t)||}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we conclude that $a(t)=5\operatorname{sin}⁡t.$
